result.description:
Motor Mechanic 
Davey Automotive Services – Breakwater, VIC, 3219
Permanent, full-time | $79,423 plus superannuation 

About us

Davey Automotive Services is a professional automotive workshop based in Breakwater, providing mechanical repairs, servicing and vehicle support for private, commercial and fleet customers.

The business specialises in scheduled servicing, diagnostics, mechanical repairs, vehicle inspections, roadworthy requirements, parts support and after-sales care. With experience across all makes and models, Davey Automotive Services delivers practical, reliable and detail-focused automotive services tailored to our customer’s needs.

The workshop is operated with a strong focus on workmanship, safety and customer confidence. Each vehicle is assessed and prepared with care to ensure it meets expected standards of performance, reliability and roadworthiness.

The role 

We are seeking a qualified and experienced Motor Mechanic to join our team. The role involves maintaining, testing, diagnosing and repairing petrol engines and the mechanical parts of lightweight motor vehicles, including transmissions, suspension, steering and braking systems.

You will be responsible for carrying out scheduled servicing, fault diagnosis, repairs, parts replacement and performance testing in accordance with manufacturer specifications, service manuals and workshop procedures. The role requires accurate diagnosis of mechanical and electrical faults, safe dismantling and reassembly of vehicle components, and the use of appropriate hand tools, workshop equipment and computer-based diagnostic systems.

The successful candidate will be expected to work efficiently within a busy workshop, maintain accurate records of work completed, support the preparation and ongoing servicing of vehicles, and ensure all work is completed safely and to the required standard.

Flexibility is essential, as the role may involve working across business operating hours, including Saturdays.

Key duties and responsibilities 

- Maintain, test and repair petrol engines and mechanical components of lightweight motor vehicles.
- Detect and diagnose mechanical and electrical faults in engines, transmissions, suspension, steering, braking systems and related vehicle components.
- Use computer-based diagnostic equipment, testing procedures and road testing where required to identify faults and confirm repair outcomes.
- Dismantle and remove engine assemblies, transmissions, steering mechanisms and other components, and inspect parts for wear, damage or defects.
- Repair, adjust or replace worn, damaged or defective parts and reassemble mechanical components with reference to service manuals and manufacturer specifications.
- Perform scheduled maintenance services, including oil changes, lubrication, filter replacement, safety checks and engine tune-ups, to support smooth vehicle operation and compliance with pollution requirements.
- Reassemble engines and mechanical parts after repairs have been completed.
- Test and adjust repaired mechanical parts and systems to ensure proper performance, roadworthiness and safe operation. 
- Inspect vehicles and identify work required to achieve roadworthiness, where required and where permitted by applicable regulatory requirements.
- Maintain accurate records of inspections, servicing, repairs, parts used and work completed.
- Maintain a clean, organised and safe workshop and ensure compliance with workplace health and safety requirements at all times.

Required qualifications and experience 

- Certificate III in automotive mechanical technology at least two (2) years of relevant experience; or
- Certificate IV or higher in automotive mechanical technology and at least one (1) year of relevant experience; or
- At least three (3) years of highly relevant work experience may substitute for the above formal qualifications.

How to apply 

We welcome applications from all appropriately qualified candidates. We are committed to a fair, inclusive recruitment process, and we will consider applicants based on skills, experience and role requirements.

Please submit your application through the recruitment platform for this advertisement.
Your application should include:

- A current resume outlining your relevant qualifications and work experience; and 
- A brief cover letter addressing your suitability for the role. 

To ensure all applications are properly received and assessed, please submit your application via one platform only and do not to apply through multiple job portals.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Position: Office Manager 
Office Location: 60 South Street, Ipswich QLD 4305 
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent, Minimum 38 hours a week  
Salary Package: $75,000 – $95,000 per annum (plus superannuation)

Our client PRITHVEER PTY LTD is an established Australian transport and logistics provider based out of Ipswich, Queensland, operating since 2014. They specialise in delivering goods across hospitality and healthcare sector, supported by a dedicated vehicle fleet delivering general freight, palletised freight, same-day/next-day services. They require dedicated experienced Office Manager to oversee the office and administrative backbone of the business.

Responsibilities
The Office Manager is responsible for overseeing and coordinating the daily administrative operations of the business, ensuring effective communication and workflow between office, warehouse, and fleet functions. The role involves developing and improving office systems, managing administrative staff, preparing rosters and schedules, recruitment and training, and maintaining efficient office resources. Manages budgets, financial records, and compliance requirements to support smooth freight operations, fleet administration, and the overall performance of the business.

Key Duties 
•	Plan, organise, direct and coordinate the day-to-day administrative operations of the business office, managing office procedures, correspondence, office records, and information flow between administration, dispatch, and fleet teams.
•	Develop, implement and review office systems, policies and administrative procedures to improve operational efficiency, document control, customer service processes, and internal communication across the business.
•	Liaise and coordinate with administrative staff and director, prepare workflow, and coordinate workload requirements to support freight, delivery, and business operations.
•	Oversee recruitment, onboarding, induction, and training coordination for office staffs, ensuring staff are appropriately supported and aligned with company procedures and operational requirements.
•	Maintain supplier records, and other administrative information systems to ensure accuracy, accessibility, and compliance with company requirements.
•	Manage office budgets, process financial administration activities, monitor expenditure, coordinate invoicing and accounts administration, and maintain financial records in conjunction with management and external accountant.
•	Coordinate procurement, inventory control, and distribution of office supplies, stationery, equipment, and administrative resources to ensure the office operates efficiently and effectively.
•	Manage communication with suppliers and internal stakeholders, including handling enquiries, and supporting service delivery requirements for the customers.
•	Coordinate workplace facilities, office equipment, and administrative service requirements and supplier services to support a safe and productive working environment.
•	Monitor administrative compliance requirements, maintain company documentation, support audits and reporting processes, and provide management with administrative information to assist decision-making.

Required Qualification & Experience
•	Minimum AQF Associate Diploma or Higher-level Degree in related field; and
•	A minimum of 1-year relevant experience

Salary Package: $75,000 – $95,000 per annum, commensurate with skills and experience.

Application Timeframe: 28 July 2026 to 27 August 2026. 
Interested candidates should submit their resume and cover letter. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the interview.

The Client 

A1 Brar Indian Restaurant & Sweets is a locally-owned Indian cuisine business located in Shepparton in VIC. They are currently looking for an experienced Chef to join their team. 

 

The Role 

You will have the opportunity to work in a truly dynamic team and you will have the chance to display your creativity in the dishes that you create. You will also have the opportunity to progress through the ranks at the restaurant.  

This is a full-time role with an annual salary set at $80,000 plus superannuation, depending on experience. 

 

Responsibilities 

Manage and supervise culinary staff including cooks and food preparation workers. 

Inspect the levels of ingredients, raw food supplies and other raw materials and ensure optimum stock levels 

Give orders for required supplies and making necessary requisitions for the required stock, frozen food items, beverages and other raw materials 

Inspect the received products for their quality, quantity and other attributes 

Schedule food production and managing schedule of operations through optimum use of resources and materials  

Assist kitchen staff in overall kitchen operations to ensure timely services 

Observe methods of food preparation being used by the food preparation team to ensure consistency  

Designate and assign duties based on personal capacity and capabilities, with respect to preparation of ingredients, cooking and delivery of food items 

Inspect and make use of various cooking appliances for completion of orders, inspecting the appliances for cleanliness, functionality and usability 

Perform other inventory duties, performing stock rotation 

Plan and review menus with management and actively participate in assigning prices to menu items, based on food and labour cost analysis and other overheads. 

Guiding and mentoring the employees, identifying and providing solutions for any potential issues and worker grievances 

Consistently ensure high levels of cleanliness, organization, storage and sanitation  

Ensuring that kitchen workers maintain personal hygiene and follow the cleanliness and sanitation standards 

Ensure food items being prepared are prepared within the established food preparation, portion control and pricing policies. 

Manage relationships with distributors and resolve issues with vendors promptly. 

Follow the budget established by the restaurant manager. 

Ensure safety and sanitation practices in the kitchen. 

Manage kitchen staff and delegate tasks related to meal prep, cooking and delivering food to diners in a timely fashion 

 

Requirements 

Strong food knowledge and skills in authentic Indian cuisine  

Relevant qualifications in cookery or hospitality  

At least 3 years of experience as a Chef in a similar role 

At least 3 years experience in tandoori cooking  

At least 3 years experience in preparing advanced marinades, masalas and curry pastes and sauces from scratch 

At least 3 years experience preparing and cooking Indian breads  

At least 3 years experience operating and maintaining traditional clay tandoor ovens 

Must be able to work with proteins like beef, mutton and pork 

Passion for great food and presentation 

Understanding of, and commitment to, food safety 

Experience in kitchen operations and in managing a team 

Experience in training kitchen staff 

Ability to work well under pressure 

Goods ordering and menu costing

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     HammondCare Waratah is currently looking for a Weekend Cook-Chef to join our team.

HammondCare has a unique model of care which places the resident's needs as our number one priority.

As a part of the Support Service's Team, you will support our model of care by delivering high quality meals within the MAIN KITCHEN at our Waratah Facility catering for our 232 residents in accordance with the organisational mission and mission in action statement.

Core Responsibilities:

Reporting to the Support Services Manager you will be responsible for;

Preparing nourishing, appetising, and culturally appropriate meals that meet individual dietary needs and preferences. This includes ensuring meals are visually appealing and served at the correct portion size and temperature.

Ensuring strict adherence to the Food Safety Program (FSP), HACCP standards, and all relevant health and safety regulations. This also involves complying with the Aged Care Quality Standards, specifically Standard 6: Food and nutrition.

Preparing residents' specific dietary requirements, including texture-modified food for those with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia).

Responding to feedback and addressing concerns promptly.

Maintaining accurate documentation related to food safety, resident dietary needs, and operational data.

To be successful in this role, you will:

Be flexible and able to commit to a range of shifts including weekends.

Value teamwork but also be able to work independently and show initiative.

Must have experience in cooking for large numbers in a commercial kitchen and or an aged care environment.

Have an understanding of The vulnerable persons guidelines for food safety or willingness to learn and incorporate these into your everyday work routine.

Demonstrated understanding of safe manual handling practices.

Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Experience in preparing and cooking bulk meals.

What are the benefits of working with HammondCare?

Flexible working environment to deliver a healthy work-life balance.

Gain access to multiple health and fitness facilities at a low fee with Fitness Passport

Be supported & empowered in your role to really make a difference to our residents.

A workplace trainer on each site committed to your ongoing training & development.

Access to not-for-profit salary sacrificing arrangements.
